record.paper_title: Infrared tip-tilt sensing: on-sky experience, lessons learned and unsolved problems
record.original_question: How should a laser-guide-star adaptive-optics system combine two or more off-axis infrared tip-tilt measurements to estimate the on-axis tip-tilt when the guide stars have different magnitudes, are measured at different frame rates, and have different centroiding errors caused by both photon count and spot shape? The desired solution should go beyond a weighted average by using tomography or an equivalent controller or reconstructor that can work for single-conjugate adaptive optics or laser-tomography adaptive optics.

evidence.quote: The LTAO design calls for the use of two or three tip-tilt stars in order to reduce the eﬀect of tip-tilt anisoplanatism. The capability to use multiple ROIs is already present; how to optimally combine the measurements is work in progress, and this is discussed in Section 5.2. Currently, the measurements from multiple stars can only be combined using a weighted average, 15 and an upgrade to real-time controller code is needed to support tomography.

The minimum variance reconstructor leads to optimal open-loop estimates, and this reconstructor can be used in closed-loop. However, it is not clear how to optimally combine tip-tilt measurements for the general case where two or more stars with very diﬀerent magnitudes are read at diﬀerent frame rates.

Further work on multi-rate controllers for single-conjugate adaptive optics systems is required. To be useful for NIR TTSs, these controllers should consider that measurements using oﬀ-axis stars are also have a centroiding error that depends on the shape of the spot on the detector, not just on the number of photons detected.
There are still a number of unsolved research problems and these are listed here: – Optimal on-axis tip-tilt estimates from two or more tip-tilt measurements at diﬀerent frame rates.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a laser-guide-star adaptive-optics (AO) system on a large ground-based telescope, in either single-conjugate (SCAO) or laser-tomography (LTAO) configuration. Because a sodium or Rayleigh laser-guide star is insensitive to global tip and tilt (the two lowest-order Zernike modes corresponding to angular displacement of the wavefront), the on-axis tip-tilt component of the wavefront aberration must be measured from one or more off-axis natural guide stars (NGSs), typically in the near-infrared.

Setup. Suppose K ≥ 2 NGSs at angular positions θ_1, …, θ_K relative to the science target are available. For each star k:
- the apparent magnitude m_k (and hence photon flux) differs across stars;
- the tip-tilt sensor for star k is read out at its own frame rate f_k (chosen so that enough photons are integrated per frame);
- each centroid measurement y_k(t) ∈ ℝ^2 of the two-axis image position has measurement noise with covariance R_k that depends both on the photon count per frame and on the shape (size, elongation, asymmetry) of the point-spread function on the detector;
- the relation between the on-axis tip-tilt α(t) ∈ ℝ^2 to be estimated and y_k(t) is governed by the atmospheric tip-tilt anisoplanatism kernel determined by the C_n^2(h) profile and the offsets θ_k.

Model the time evolution of the atmospheric tip-tilt and the off-axis tip-tilts as a (possibly multi-layer) stochastic process with known second-order statistics (e.g., a Kolmogorov / von Kármán turbulence model with given outer scale L_0 and layer wind velocities), so that the joint process {α(t), (y_k(t))_k} is wide-sense stationary with computable spatio-temporal covariances.

Problem. Construct a real-time controller/reconstructor 𝒦 that takes as input the asynchronous, multi-rate streams (y_k(t_{k,j}))_{k,j} and produces an on-axis tip-tilt estimate α̂(t) (or equivalent control command for the tip-tilt mirror) which is optimal in the minimum-mean-square-error sense, generalizing the simple inverse-noise-variance weighted average. Specifically:

(a) Derive a tomographic minimum-variance reconstructor that simultaneously accounts for (i) different magnitudes m_k, (ii) different sampling rates f_k, (iii) measurement-noise covariances R_k that depend on both photon count and spot shape, and (iv) tip-tilt anisoplanatism between the off-axis NGS directions θ_k and the science direction.

(b) Show how 𝒦 can be implemented in closed loop (where the deformable/tip-tilt mirror modifies the measurements) for both SCAO and LTAO architectures, and prove (or characterize) its optimality with respect to on-axis residual tip-tilt variance.

(c) Quantify the performance gain over the standard inverse-variance weighted average of the off-axis centroids as a function of the asterism geometry, the magnitude/frame-rate distribution {(m_k, f_k)}, and the turbulence profile.

A complete solution consists of an explicit reconstructor (filter equations or state-space controller), a proof of its optimality under the stated stochastic model, and a quantitative performance comparison.
artifact.status_search_result: Multi-rate, minimum-variance split-tomography reconstructors for LGS adaptive optics with dim NGS tip-tilt stars have been studied (e.g., Gilles–Wang for TMT NFIRAOS), giving partial solutions for specific instruments. However, a general optimal real-time controller that simultaneously handles multiple NGSs of different magnitudes, different frame rates, and centroid noise depending on PSF shape (not just photon count) for SCAO/LTAO remains an active and unresolved research problem.

status_evidence.title: Minimum Variance Split Tomography for Laser Guide Star Adaptive Optics
status_evidence.snippet: Split tomography architecture with separate LGS and NGS control loops; multi-rate Monte Carlo simulations for TMT NFIRAOS demonstrate the potential of minimum variance split tomography.
status_evidence.claim: Partial solutions exist for specific architectures via minimum-variance split tomography, supporting that the general problem is being actively studied but not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Increased sky coverage with optimal correction of tilt and tilt-anisoplanatism modes in laser-guide-star multiconjugate adaptive optics
status_evidence.snippet: Strehl-optimal spatiotemporal reconstructors merging modal tomography and stochastic optimal control are developed for tilt and tilt-anisoplanatism modes in LGS MCAO.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal spatiotemporal tilt reconstructors have been developed in the MCAO setting, but extension to general multi-rate, shape-dependent NGS noise in SCAO/LTAO is still incomplete.
